findings.summary: gh, curl and wget are listed as write programs, but they are not; refusing them depends on the grant, which goes against the plan's own 'grant-independent' rule.
findings.evidence: The plan says 'the write lists are fixed facts about writing, not copies of a grant'. But `gh run view`, `gh pr view`, `curl <url>` and `wget -O- <url>` only read. Whether the verifier may run them depends on the target's verifier_commands, which athena.toml:76/108 set per capability. Round 4 dropped the hand-copied table so that a target with a wider grant is not refused. A target that grants `gh = ["run"]` to check CI would still be refused for 'Run `gh run view`: the run passed', and the error would wrongly say the program writes. Fix: Take gh, curl and wget out of the write-program list, or move them into the named follow-up (judging them against the live grant). Then the doc comment and D174 can honestly claim that rule (3) holds for every grant. If the producer keeps them, the plan should call them a deliberate grant-dependent exception and list them among the known misses or false positives.
findings.location: Decision 3, rule (3) write programs; Decision 6 error text

findings.summary: An edit verb aimed at the decision this job is itself appending (for example 'Update D174 ...') is refused, because without the marker nothing tells an existing id from a new one.
findings.evidence: Rule (i) refuses an edit verb in verb position followed by an id, with only entry words between, in a clause that holds a decision-log word. 'Fix the D174 decision so its link line matches' or 'Add to D174 in docs/decisions.md a Provenance bullet' (rule ii) would be refused even though D174 does not exist yet. The accept list covers only append, -ed and -s phrasings. Fix: Either list this as a known false positive in D174 and the doc comment, so the reader can reword it, or skip ids above the highest `## Dnnn` heading in docs/decisions.md when repo_files gives the log. That skip is a fact read from the file, not a phrase exemption.
findings.location: Decision 4, rule (i)/(ii) with no new-id marker

findings.summary: Spell out that the words passed to cargo_subcommand exclude the program name `cargo`.
findings.evidence: policy.rs:1060-1080 and slot_exec.rs:60 pass only the words after `cargo` (for example `["--locked", "test"]`). If the full word list were passed, the call would return "cargo". Also, `cargo +nightly fmt` returns "+nightly" (policy.rs:1073), so a toolchain-prefixed fmt goes unread. Fix: In step 1, say that the call is `cargo_subcommand(&words[1..])`, and add `cargo +toolchain fmt` to the known misses.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading and grepping; I ran nothing. The plan fixes the cause where it starts: one new check, run as the last step of refusing_check (checks.rs:534-549), compares each criterion with the D43 evidence rules and the append-only rules. The names it relies on exist as stated: `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand` is public (lib.rs:16, policy.rs:519), INPUT_FORMS is `[&str; 63]`, READING_RULES is `[&str; 12]`, the baseline is 3045 bytes, D173 is the last decision, and the only existing cited write command is the `git push` text at reading.rs:5094, which the plan moves into its own test. Grep shows no other existing accept text that cites a git or cargo write subcommand, an env prefix or a plain `cargo fmt`, and no test criterion that the decision-id rule would newly refuse. The dependents list covers every caller of refusing_check, check_reading_acceptance and check_reading_text (steward.rs, replay.rs, run, cli main.rs and drain). Each criterion's demonstration goes through a production seam (gate_refuser/refusing_check, replay_declaration, reader_brief, check_log) and would fail without the change. The matcher is lexical, but it follows the phrase-matching style of check_criteria_evidence, needs a verb in verb position plus decision-log context, and lists its known misses. One remaining soundness flaw: gh, curl and wget are called write programs although they can read and the verifier's grant decides whether they may run. That flaw, the possible false refusal of edits to the job's own new decision, and a cargo_subcommand calling detail are all minor.
